docs.text: This code imports the create_model function from the trano.main module and calls it to create a model based on a specified YAML configuration file and a library.

docs.title: General Description and Parameters
docs.text:
• Function: create_model
  • Parameters:
  • path_to_yaml_configuration_folder / "zone_with_ventilation.yaml": Path to the YAML configuration file describing the model.
  • library="iso_13790": Specifies the library to use for creating the model, in this case, the ISO 13790 standard.

The figure below illustrates the generated model, highlighting the subcomponent related to ventilation.

Opening the ventilation component reveals the various elements associated with the ventilation system.

docs.title: ASHRAE 140 (BESTEST) validation
docs.text:
The building models trano generates are validated against the 27 cases of section 5.2 of ASHRAE Standard 140-2020 (the BESTEST single-zone cases): a 8 m x 6 m x 2.7 m zone in Denver with light or heavy constructions, 12 m2 of double glazing, 0.414 air changes per hour of infiltration and 200 W of internal gains, with variants for the insulation, the glazing, the window orientation, overhangs and side fins, an unconditioned sun-space, free-floating temperatures, a dual set point ideal system with set-backs and night ventilation.

Each case is a trano YAML file (validation/bestest/cases/), simulated for a year with each library. The annual heating and cooling loads must fall inside the acceptance limits of the standard; the peak loads and the free-floating temperatures must fall inside the spread of the reference programs (BSIMAC, CSE, DeST, EnergyPlus, ESP-r, TRNSYS) widened by 5 % of the largest peak or 1 K. Buildings, IDEAS and FastSmoothBuildings are gating libraries: pytest -m bestest fails when one of their cases leaves its band, except for the deviations listed below with their reason; FastSmoothBuildings, the reduced library of trano that translates to CasADi, has its own section. The reduced-order (AixLib) and ISO 13790 zones are shown for information: ISO 13790 is a monthly method applied hour by hour and the reduced-order zone still deviates on several cases, so neither gates. Cases a library cannot describe (shading with IDEAS, which OpenModelica cannot compile for IDEAS 3.0.0; shading, sun-space and night ventilation with the two simplified zones) are left out. The tables are rendered from the last results with python -m validation.bestest report --docs. A walk through the BESTEST cases explains a few cases in detail: what they are, what is expected, how the YAML describes them and how the results compare.

docs.title: FastSmoothBuildings
docs.text:
The FastSmoothBuildings library is trano's reduced model of the same building: the closed-loop model whose components rumoca translates to a CasADi ODE for optimal control and calibration. It runs the same YAML files in OpenModelica. Its walls are discretised as Buildings discretises them (number_of_states, at most three sublayers per layer), its zones take the air density of the site and exchange long-wave radiation as the YAML asks (linearised at 20 degC or around the current surface temperatures), its outer surfaces exchange with sky and ground exactly, the gas gaps of its glazings conduct at the temperatures of their panes (long-wave exchange and convection of the gas, as Buildings), its windows are shaded by overhangs and side fins as in Buildings, and its controllers are smooth and without events. It gates as Buildings and IDEAS do, on the 27 cases. The column Buildings gives the frozen value of Buildings for the same case (expected/Buildings.json), so that the gap between the two libraries reads next to the band. How the two libraries compare hour by hour, and how they respond to a change of the parameters, is studied in the documentation of FastSmoothBuildings; how the library came to these results is told in its improvement plan.

105 of 105 KPIs of 27 cases are inside their band. Against Buildings, the loads differ by 1.1 % on average and 4.4 % at most, the temperatures of the free-floating zones by 0.38 K on average and 1.70 K at most.

docs.title: A walk through the BESTEST cases
docs.text:
The validation page lists every KPI of every case. This page takes a few cases and tells, for each of them, what the case is, what the six reference programs of ASHRAE Standard 140-2020 (BSIMAC, CSE, DeST, EnergyPlus, ESP-r and TRNSYS) expect, how the trano YAML describes the case and how the results of each library compare with that expectation. The YAML fragments are cut out of the generated case files in validation/bestest/cases/, the tables and the charts are rendered from the reference data and the last results, with python -m validation.bestest report --docs.

A band is the range a result must fall in: the acceptance limits of the standard for the annual loads, and the spread of the reference programs widened by 5 % of the largest peak (loads) or by 1 K (temperatures) otherwise. In the result tables, ✓ marks a value inside its band, ~ a known deviation documented on the validation page and ✗ a value outside its band. Buildings and IDEAS gate the test suite; the reduced-order (AixLib) and ISO 13790 zones are shown for information.

docs.title: Case 600: Base case, low mass
docs.text: The base case: a single rectangular zone of 8 m by 6 m by 2.7 m in Denver (cold, sunny, 1609 m above sea level) with light-weight walls (wood siding, fibreglass, plasterboard), a light roof and a timber floor over 1 m of insulation whose underside sees the outdoor air. The south wall carries 12 m2 of clear double glazing without any frame. Infiltration is 0.414 air changes per hour (0.5 at sea level, corrected for the altitude), the internal gains are 200 W around the clock (60 % radiant, 40 % convective) and an ideal system keeps the air between 20 degC (heating) and 27 degC (cooling) with unlimited capacity.

docs.title: What the reference programs expect
docs.text:
KPI BSIMAC CSE DeST EnergyPlus ESP-r TRNSYS Band annual heating [MWh] 4.050 3.993 4.047 4.324 4.362 4.504 3.750 to 4.980 (limits of the standard) annual cooling [MWh] 5.822 5.913 5.432 6.027 6.162 5.780 5.000 to 6.830 (limits of the standard) peak heating [kW] 3.255 3.020 3.035 3.204 3.228 3.359 2.852 to 3.527 (programs ± tolerance) peak cooling [kW] 5.650 6.481 5.422 6.352 6.193 6.046 5.098 to 6.805 (programs ± tolerance)

Winter nights drive the heating, so the heating peak falls on the coldest hours of January or December. The cooling peak falls on a sunny winter day too: the low sun pours through the south glazing and the light envelope has nothing to store it in, so the zone hits 27 degC within a few hours. The annual loads must fall inside the acceptance limits of the standard; the peaks must fall inside the spread of the reference programs widened by 5 % of the largest peak. The hourly loads of 1 February are compared as well: a cold clear day on which the zone switches from heating at night to cooling around noon.

docs.title: How the YAML describes it
docs.text:
The zone is a space with the infiltration variant, whose ach parameter is the air change rate; linearize_emissive_power: false keeps the long-wave exchange non-linear as the standard asks. The floor is a floor_on_grounds boundary with the outdoor_air variant (its outer surface follows the outdoor dry-bulb temperature), the roof is an external wall with the ceiling tilt. The 200 W of internal gains are an occupancy element occupied all day, with the radiant, convective and latent gains per square metre of floor. The ideal system is the ideal_heating_cooling emission: its set points are day schedules in kelvin (time since midnight in seconds, value) repeated every day, and its capacities are 1 MW so that the set points are always met. The weather is the Denver TMY3 file shipped with Buildings; the atmospheric pressure is read from the file, so that the air density, and with it the infiltration mass flow, is that of the site. Every material has 18 states per 0.2 m of layer (number_of_states), the discretisation of Buildings' own BESTEST models.

weather:

parameters:
  path: Modelica.Utilities.Files.loadResource("modelica://Buildings/Resources/weatherdata/USA_CO_Denver.Intl.AP.725650_TMY3.mos")
  atmospheric_pressure_source: Buildings.BoundaryConditions.Types.DataSource.File

docs.text: Case 600 without any heating or cooling: the temperature of the zone floats freely under the weather and the internal gains.

docs.title: Case 900: Base case, high mass
docs.text: Case 600 with heavy constructions: the walls are concrete blocks behind foam insulation and wood siding, the floor is a concrete slab over the insulation. The U-values are the same as in case 600; only the thermal mass changes.

docs.title: What the reference programs expect
docs.text:

The mass stores the solar gains of the day and gives them back at night, so both the heating and the cooling loads drop a lot against case 600, the cooling by more than half. The peaks drop too, and the heating peak moves to the end of long cold spells rather than to the first cold night. The hourly loads of 1 February show a much smoother profile than case 600.

The annual heating is zero by construction. docs.title: How the YAML describes it
docs.text:
The fan is the ventilation_schedule parameter of the space: a day schedule of outdoor air mass flow in kg/s brought in on top of the infiltration, at the outdoor temperature and humidity, 1409 kg/h being 1700 m3/h at the air density of the site. The heating is switched off with a set point of 0 degC and a capacity of zero; the cooling set point is 100 degC outside the cooling hours.

docs.title: Case 960: Low mass zone with an unconditioned high mass sun-space
docs.text: A two-zone case: the back zone of case 600 keeps its light envelope but loses its windows, and a 2 m deep unconditioned sun-space with heavy walls, a concrete slab and the 12 m2 of south glazing is attached to its south wall. The two zones share a 0.2 m concrete common wall. The back zone is conditioned between 20 and 27 degC; the sun-space floats freely.

The sun-space collects the solar gains, stores them in its mass and conducts part of them through the common wall into the back zone, so the back zone needs less heating than case 600 and very little cooling. The standard checks the loads of the back zone and the maximum, minimum and mean temperature of the sun-space.

docs.title: Residential reference cases: IDEAS and Buildings
docs.text:
Two YAML files describe the same Belgian semi-detached house before and after a deep renovation:

  • examples/residential_before_renovation.yaml
  • examples/residential_after_renovation.yaml

Each file generates the model of either library, with the same geometry, zoning, use and weather:

trano create-model examples/residential_before_renovation.yaml IDEAS
trano create-model examples/residential_before_renovation.yaml Buildings

Both files are written by examples/residential_cases.py, which also prints the sizing below: change the house there, not in the YAML files.

docs.title: The house
docs.text:
Semi-detached two-storey house in Uccle, 7.4 m x 8.4 m inside, street facade north, garden facade south, gable west and party wall east. Heated floor area 110.6 m2 in six zones.

Zone Storey Floor area [m2] Height [m] Exposed surfaces Set point [degC], schedule Living (with the hall) ground 40.0 2.6 south, west, north (hall), party wall, slab 21, 7-23 h Kitchen ground 15.0 2.6 north, west, slab 21, 7-23 h Bedroom 1 first 18.5 2.5 south, west, attic floor 18, 6-23 h Bedroom 2 first 18.5 2.5 north, west, attic floor 18, 6-23 h Bedroom 3 first 9.6 2.5 north, party wall, attic floor 18, 6-23 h Bathroom first 9.0 2.5 south, party wall, attic floor 22, 6-9 h and 19-22 h

Every room falls back to 16 degC outside its schedule. Four occupants, with the default occupancy gains of trano during the occupied hours of each room. Windows: 21.1 m2 (19 % of the floor area), 6.5 m2 of them facing the garden. The ceiling of the first floor is the floor of a cold, ventilated attic, modelled as a roof towards the outdoor air.

The party wall is an adiabatic wall (new, see below): half of the 19 cm brick wall, whose mid-plane is adiabatic because the neighbour is heated alike.

docs.title: Envelope
docs.text:
Element Before renovation U [W/(m2.K)] After renovation U [W/(m2.K)] External wall brick cavity wall, 5 cm air cavity 1.47 + 12 cm EPS (ETICS) 0.23 Attic floor timber floor on joists 1.70 + 22 cm mineral wool 0.15 Slab on ground concrete and tiles 3.43 (slab), 0.71 (with the ground, ISO 13370) + 8 cm PUR 0.27 (slab), 0.20 (with the ground) Windows double glazing 4-12-4 air, wooden frames Ug 2.88, Uw 2.71, g 0.76 triple glazing argon, two low-e coatings, insulated frames Ug 0.70, Uw 0.80, g 0.47 Airtightness n50 = 12 1/h (0.6 1/h of infiltration) n50 = 3 1/h (0.15 1/h)

The glazings are described by their panes and gaps: trano computes U and g (EN 673, EN 410) for IDEAS from the same layers that Buildings uses, so that both libraries see the same windows. Air layers in opaque constructions are equivalent conductivities giving the EN ISO 6946 resistance of an unventilated cavity (0.18 m2K/W for 5 cm, 0.16 m2K/W between the joists).

Before renovation After renovation Design heat loss 10.75 kW (97 W/m2) 2.34 kW (21 W/m2) Generator non-condensing gas boiler, 16 kW (1.4 x the loss, reheat after the setback), efficiency 0.85 (lower heating value), 75 degC supply air-water heat pump, 3 kW at -8 degC / 40 degC (1.25 x the loss), heating curve 40 degC at -8 degC to 30 degC at 16 degC outdoor, 100 l buffer Emission radiators rated 1.2 x the room loss at 75/65/20 degC, 13.2 kW in total, thermostatic valves (P control) the same radiators: they cover the loss of every room from 39 degC supply Ventilation natural, by infiltration balanced with heat recovery (system D), 150 m3/h (0.5 1/h), effectiveness 0.8, supply and extract in every room PV - 21 m2 of 20 % modules (4.2 kWp), south, 35 degrees Room Design loss before [W] Design loss after [W] Radiator at 75/65/20 degC [W] Living 3239 815 3900 Kitchen 1446 355 1800 Bedroom 1 2059 387 2500 Bedroom 2 2078 396 2500 Bedroom 3 921 179 1200 Bathroom 1006 204 1300

docs.title: Reference examples
docs.text:
The systems follow these examples of the libraries trano targets (IDEAS 3.0.0, Buildings 13.0.0):

  • IDEAS.Examples.PPD12 (a Belgian terraced house of about 120 m2): zoning, party walls as BoundaryWalls, radiators RadiatorEN442_2 rated at 75/65/20 degC, a gas boiler of 30 kW at 70 degC, balanced ventilation with a ConstantEffectiveness heat exchanger (0.75) and 300 m3/h.
  • Buildings.Fluid.HeatPumps.ModularReversible.Examples.AirToWater2D_OneRoomRadiator: the air-water heat pump (AirToWaterTableData2D, Vitocal 251-A data), its safety control (Wuellhorst2021, minimum on and off times) and its own condenser pump; trano's heat pump now follows it (see below).
  • Buildings.Examples.HydronicHeating.TwoRoomsWithStorage: BoilerPolynomial, radiators with two-way valves and balanced ventilation with heat recovery (0.9).
  • Buildings.Examples.Tutorial.SimpleHouse.SimpleHouse6: heat recovery ventilation (0.85).
  • Buildings.Electrical.AC.OnePhase.Sources (PVSimpleOriented): the PV array.

Neither library has a dwelling that combines a heat pump with PV: the after-renovation case is new.

docs.title: Component mapping
docs.text:
The hydronic and ventilation systems of trano are built from Buildings components in the models of both libraries (the Trano package of every model); the envelope, the zones, the weather and the radiators come from the library chosen.

docs.title: Changes to trano for these cases
docs.text:
The cases revealed problems in the existing models of trano, fixed along with the extensions:

  • Air-water heat pump rebuilt on the Buildings reference example: it could not start with Buildings 13 (swapped cooling temperatures), had no safety control and no condenser pump of its own, and drew its heat from a constant 10 degC source, so its water boiled when the radiator valves closed. It now charges a buffer through its own pump, follows a heating curve, keeps the library's safety control and takes the outdoor air as source (heat_pump_source_outdoor_air, true by default).
  • Boilers fire on heat demand only; the casing loss defaults to 0.5 % of the nominal power at 50 K instead of 5 % at 30 K; natural gas counts on its lower heating value for every variant.
  • Outputs on the data bus: electrical power and energy of the heat pump and of the ventilation fans (in the grid load), fuel power and energy of the boilers, heat delivered, supply and return temperatures, PV production.
  • Adiabatic walls (external_boundaries.adiabatic_walls) for party walls, in IDEAS, Buildings, the reduced-order and the ISO 13790 zones.
  • IDEAS ground model: average_indoor_temperature of a floor on ground sets the room temperature of the ISO 13370 heat flow of IDEAS (22 degC otherwise).
  • Same defaults in every library: the Uccle weather of IDEAS when none is given, the infiltration of the IDEAS zones (0.15 1/h) for the Buildings infiltration variant, and 21 degC as the default heating set point.

All of them are optional: models that do not use them only change where a default was wrong.

docs.title: Results over a year
docs.text:
Both cases simulated over a year in OpenModelica 1.26 (IDEAS 3.0.0, Buildings 13.0.0) with the Uccle weather of IDEAS (11.1 degC mean). Energies are taken from the counters each element puts on the data bus; the heat of the radiators is integrated from their heat flows.

Before, Buildings Before, IDEAS Difference After, Buildings After, IDEAS Difference Heat from the radiators [kWh] 14 420 14 910 +3.4 % 1 952 1 809 -7.3 % Heating demand [kWh/m2] 130 135 17.6 16.4 Heat from the generator [kWh] 15 591 15 845 +1.6 % 1 992 1 844 -7.4 % Gas, lower heating value [kWh] 19 188 19 361 +0.9 % - - Heat pump electricity [kWh] - - 529 494 -6.6 % Seasonal COP of the heat pump - - 3.77 3.73 -0.9 % Ventilation fans [kWh] - - 224 224 0.0 % Circulation pumps [kWh] 30 27 17 16 PV production [kWh] - - 4 644 4 645 0.0 %

The two libraries agree on the annual heating within 3.4 % before and 7.3 % after renovation, within the 10 % aimed at. Per room:

Room Radiators before, Buildings / IDEAS [kWh] Difference Radiators after, Buildings / IDEAS [kWh] Difference Living 4 639 / 4 612 -1 % 806 / 757 -6 % Kitchen 2 579 / 2 691 +4 % 607 / 561 -8 % Bedroom 1 2 130 / 2 237 +5 % 67 / 54 -19 % Bedroom 2 2 594 / 2 770 +7 % 157 / 140 -11 % Bedroom 3 1 170 / 1 236 +6 % 46 / 38 -17 % Bathroom 1 308 / 1 364 +4 % 267 / 258 -3 %

After renovation the bedrooms, at 18 degC, are kept warm by the rooms around them and by the supply air: their few tens of kWh differ by up to 19 % between the libraries without weighing on the total.

The renovation cuts the heat delivered to the rooms by 86 % (130 to 18 kWh/m2) and the final energy for heating from 19.2 MWh of gas to 0.53 MWh of electricity. With the fans, the house draws 0.75 MWh of electricity a year for heating and ventilation, against 4.6 MWh produced by the PV, most of it from April to September (see the tutorial for the monthly figures).

docs.title: Known differences and limits
docs.text:
• Ground. IDEAS computes the heat flow through the slab with the ISO 13370 model, from the exposed perimeter and the mean temperature of the room above; Buildings holds the outer face of the slab at a fixed temperature. examples/residential_cases.py sets that temperature so that both lose the same heat over the heating season. The IDEAS ground starts at 10.8 degC and takes about two weeks to settle: short simulations (the four January days of tests/test_residential_examples.py) differ more (within 15 % upstairs, 25 % for the house).
  • Comfort in the bathroom after renovation. The bathroom (22 degC, 6-9 h and 19-22 h, 16 degC otherwise) is below 21 degC during 43 % of its occupied hours in both libraries: the radiator kept from before the renovation warms it slowly from the setback with water at 30-40 degC. A lighter setback, an earlier start or a towel radiator sized for low temperatures would fix it; the case keeps the radiators on purpose. The other rooms are below their set point minus 1 K during at most 8 % of their occupied hours before renovation (the reheat after the setback) and 4 % after.
  • Boiler losses. BoilerPolynomial of Buildings 13 subtracts the loss of its casing twice from the water; trano sets that loss to 0.5 % of the nominal power at 50 K so that it stays small. Before renovation, 7.5 % of the heat of the boiler is lost by the boiler, the pipes and the valves before the radiators.
  • Air layers of opaque constructions are equivalent solid layers in both libraries (no convection or radiation across the cavity).
  • Natural ventilation before renovation is the infiltration of the zones, constant at n50 / 20; it does not vary with the wind or the temperature difference.

docs.title: Simulation performance
docs.text:
Envelope-only models generated by trano simulate a week in about a second; the same buildings with a hydronic heating system take ten to two hundred times longer. This page explains where the time goes, which simplifications trano applies by default to reduce it (and how to turn them off), what they cost in accuracy, and what remains inherent to the libraries. The numbers are measured by a reproducible benchmark:

TRANO_MODELICA_LIBRARIES=<installed libraries> python -m validation.performance \
    --profiles baseline fast hysteresis fast_hysteresis

docs.title: Diagnosis method
docs.text:
Each model is translated with buildModel and its executable run on its own, so that the translation (OpenModelica front end, back end, code generation and C compilation) and the simulation are timed separately. The settings are fixed: DASSL, tolerance 1e-6, one week from 1 January (Uccle weather), one output point every 15 minutes, OpenModelica 1.26.9 with Buildings 13.0.0, IDEAS 3.0.0 and the Modelica Standard Library 4.1.0.

The statistics behind the diagnosis come from OpenModelica itself:

  • -d=backenddaeinfo at translation: number of states and size of the linear and nonlinear systems left after tearing;
  • -lv=LOG_STATS,LOG_STATS_V at simulation: steps, right-hand-side and Jacobian evaluations, error and convergence test failures, state and time events, time spent in each linear and nonlinear system;
  • -lv=LOG_EVENTS: which zero-crossing triggers each event;
  • -noEquidistantTimeGrid: every accepted step written to the result, to see where the steps are small.

Controlled experiments then change one aspect of the generated model at a time and measure the effect on speed and on the results.

docs.title: Where the time goes
docs.text:
envelope only with hydronic heating steps per simulated week about 1 900 22 000 to 42 000 median step about 300 s 1.9 s state events per week 0 to 14 330 to 1 080 share of the simulation time spent in Jacobian evaluations small 74 % (single zone) to 88 % (house)

Buildings and IDEAS are equally slow for the same hydronic system: the cost comes from the hydronic components trano shares between the libraries, not from the envelope models. Four causes were found.

Actuator filters inside control loops (trano modelling default). Every valve and pump keeps the filter of its library approximating the actuator's stroke time (120 s) or the mover's rise time (30 s), and the temperature sensors keep a first-order lag of 1 s. The valves and pumps sit in proportional or PI loops on the zone temperature and on the loop pressure: with the filters, these loops force steps of about 2 s for the whole simulation and trigger many convergence test failures, each of which costs a new Jacobian.

Costly Jacobians. DASSL evaluates its Jacobian numerically, one model evaluation per colour of the sparsity pattern (about 20 to 45). Each evaluation solves the algebraic loop of the hydraulic network (the pump curve, the three-way valve and the radiator valves: a nonlinear system of 3 to 8 iteration variables and a linear system of up to 14) and, with Buildings, the long-wave radiation exchange of every room (linear systems of 10 to 24 unknowns per room). The number of Jacobians is set by the step failures and the events.

Events of the controls (trano modelling default). The boiler control compares the tank temperatures with fixed thresholds without hysteresis and waits on state-graph timers: in the three-zone model it causes 585 of the 913 events of a week, about 3.5 threshold crossings per burner cycle. The G36 zone controller of the radiator valves adds about 100 events per zone and week (enable hysteresis, PI reset, timers). After the filters are removed, a third of all steps are the small steps following an event.

Translation (library and tool). 35 s to 220 s, of which about 7 s load the libraries and 10 s to 25 s compile the C code. It does not depend on the options below.

Solver settings were measured as well and are not worth changing: a tolerance of 1e-4 saves about 20 % with DASSL, CVODE is 20 % faster on one model and 60 % slower on another (and fails on a pump efficiency assertion at zero speed with a tolerance of 1e-4), a symbolic Jacobian saves at most 10 %, the sparse linear solvers fail at initialization, and the output interval is negligible (writing the result takes less than 0.3 s).

docs.title: Ideal actuators and steady-state sensors (on by default)
docs.text:
Both options are on by default. To generate the detailed model, with the actuator and sensor dynamics of the libraries, turn them off in the YAML (an option left out of the block stays on):

performance:
  ideal_actuators: false       # keep the stroke-time and rise-time filters of valves, dampers, pumps, fans
  steady_state_sensors: false  # keep the first-order lag of the two-port sensors

ideal_actuators sets use_strokeTime=false (Buildings, AixLib) or use_inputFilter=false (IDEAS) on every valve and damper, and use_riseTime=false or use_inputFilter=false on every pump and fan; steady_state_sensors sets tau=0 on the two-port sensors of temperature, humidity, mass fraction, trace substances, enthalpy, entropy and density. They apply to every declaration of these library classes in the generated model, including the ones of the embedded Trano package; a value set by a template or in the YAML always wins. The same options can be given in Python, where they replace those of the YAML:

from trano.data_models.conversion import convert_network
from trano.performance import PerformanceOptions

detailed = convert_network("house", path, performance=PerformanceOptions.disabled())

Why it works: without the filters the actuators are algebraic, so the loops no longer have fast closed-loop dynamics and the steps are set by the building and the events; the convergence test failures drop from hundreds to tens. The price is a larger nonlinear system of the hydraulic network (the pump speed becomes an iteration variable), which is cheaper than the steps it saves.

The two options are meant to be used together: on their own, steady-state sensors do not speed the models up (their states are cheap), but they remove the last fast states once the actuators are ideal.

Accuracy: the filters are part of the closed-loop dynamics, so removing them shifts the burner and pump cycles in time. With the boiler models the zone air temperatures deviate by up to a few tenths of a kelvin in RMSE and up to a few kelvin at the worst instant, while the delivered heating energy changes by about one percent; with the heat pump of the residential house the zone temperatures stay within 0.05 K in RMSE and 0.35 K at the worst instant. With steady-state sensors, a sensor in a pipe without flow reports the water flowing in rather than the last temperature it measured: the supply and return temperatures read at zero flow differ, the heat delivered does not. The defaults suit long simulations (annual energy, parameter studies, optimization); turn the options off to study the transients of a control loop.

docs.title: Hysteresis of the boiler control
docs.text:
systems:
  - boiler:
      id: BOILER:001
      control:
        boiler_control:
          id: BOILER_CONTROL:001
          parameters:
            temperature_hysteresis: 1.0  # [K], 0 by default

The tank temperature checks that start and stop the boiler stay true until their temperature falls temperature_hysteresis below the threshold, instead of switching at every crossing (default and complex boiler controls; the simple control of heat pumps has its own band). It removes the chattering of the checks around their threshold.

It does not change the results (zone temperatures within 0.11 K) but it does not speed the models up measurably either: it removes up to 110 of 900 events a week in the three-zone model, which is within the run-to-run noise of the timings. Use it for a cleaner burner operation, not for speed.

docs.title: Results
docs.text: Simulation of one week, translation measured once per model (the options do not change it). The timings vary by about 7 % from run to run on the same machine. Accuracy is measured against the baseline, the detailed model generated with both options off, from the second day on; tolerances: zone air temperature RMSE 0.1 K and maximum 0.5 K, heating energy 2 %. Bold deviations are beyond tolerance.

The simulation is 1.1 to 2.4 times faster: the steps are halved and the convergence failures almost disappear. The heating energy is unchanged to within 1 %. The zone temperatures stay within tolerance for the house with infiltration and for the residential house (heat pump), but not for the single and three-zone boiler models, whose burner cycles are shifted in time: up to 0.46 K RMSE and 3.1 K at the worst instant. The supply and return temperatures differ by 3 K to 60 K at the worst instant, mostly while a loop has no flow, where the steady-state sensors read the incoming water instead of holding their last value. Turn the options off when the transients of a control loop matter. The gain on the whole run is smaller where translation dominates (three-zone model with Buildings: 157 s to 143 s, translation included).

Models outside the benchmark set were checked over one day with both libraries: the ventilation models (single_zone_air_handling_unit_complex_vav, multizone_air_handling_unit_space_connected) are unchanged (zone temperatures identical to 0.01 K); the house with an air-water heat pump simulates 1.7 to 1.9 times faster (zone temperature RMSE 0.03 K, heating energy within 1.4 %). The VAV model with IDEAS did not finish one simulated day in 30 minutes with the options off; with them it takes 27 s.

The house with infiltration and the residential house are not affected (their generator controls have no tank checks). Combined with fast, the hysteresis gives the same times as fast alone. The full report, with the solver statistics of every run, is written by the benchmark to .cache/performance/report.md.

docs.title: Reproducing
docs.text:
# all models but house_complex, profiles baseline and fast, one week
TRANO_MODELICA_LIBRARIES=<installed libraries> python -m validation.performance
# one model and library, all profiles
python -m validation.performance --models three_zones_hydronic --libraries Buildings \
    --profiles baseline fast hysteresis fast_hysteresis

The runs are kept in .cache/performance/<case>/ (model, logs, results, run.json) and reused while the generated model does not change; --force runs them again, --reuse renders the report again from the stored runs. The executable resolves modelica:// URIs (the weather file) against its working directory, where the benchmark links the installed libraries.

docs.title: Remaining limits
docs.text:
• Room radiation exchange of Buildings. Each room of Buildings.ThermalZones.Detailed solves a dense linear system for the long-wave radiation between its surfaces at every model evaluation; with 6 to 11 surfaces per room it dominates the Jacobian cost of the residential house (Buildings is 2.8 times slower than IDEAS on it). Merging surfaces would shrink it, but in the houses benchmarked no two surfaces of a room share construction, orientation and neighbour, so no merge is exact; trano does not merge them.
  • Translation time is spent in OpenModelica and in the C compiler.
  • Events of the remaining controls. The heat pump's own minimum run and lock times, the buffer charging band and the G36 zone controllers still cause hundreds of events per week; they are part of the modelled behaviour.
  • Hydraulic operating point. The radiator loops run at 1 % to 10 % of the nominal flow of their pump, which is controlled by a proportional controller on the loop pressure. This is a sizing question for the model rather than a numerical setting and is left as it is.

docs.title: Systems validation
docs.text: Do the heating and ventilation systems trano generates behave as the real ones do? Each case below puts one system on the same 100 m2 zone (filled cavity walls, insulated roof and slab, 10 m2 of low-e double glazing facing south, n50 = 3, occupied from 7 to 19 h, heated to 21 degC from 7 to 22 h and 16 degC at night) for one week of the Uccle weather, and is simulated with Buildings, IDEAS and FastSmoothBuildings. The KPIs are read from the result files by validation/systems/kpi.py; the band of every KPI and the physical reasoning behind it are in validation/systems/expected.yaml; pytest -m systems fails when a KPI leaves its band. The tables are rendered from the last results with python -m validation.systems report --docs.
